scientific_object.working_title: Local Repairs, Non-Local Effects: Constraint-Coupled Externalities in Self-Evolving Agents
scientific_object.question: When a self-evolving agent performs a local benign repair, what determines whether that repair remains local or causes unintended behavioral changes elsewhere?
scientific_object.testable_question: With one update surface, backbone, harness, target repair, update artifact, constraint count, and matched pre-update difficulty held fixed, does an outcome-blind constraint-interaction topology causally change the probability that previously satisfied non-target constraints become violated?
scientific_object.paper_story_sentence: We test whether constraint coupling explains collateral effects of local self-updates.
scientific_object.forbidden_claim: We discover constraint coupling causes global interference.

constraint.definition: A semantic task obligation or invariant compiled before agent execution into a programmatically evaluable predicate phi_j over AppWorld initial/final database state and, only where required, declared trajectory/interaction state. Multiple raw assertions that implement one obligation must be grouped into one ConstraintSpec rather than counted as independent constraints.

interaction_edge.definition: An edge between c_j and c_k is declared before model outcomes when their static ConstraintSpecs share a causal resource or explicit prerequisite: overlapping mutable database entity/table/field, a state-changing API with overlapping resource footprint, or a directed temporal/read-after-write prerequisite. Semantic similarity alone and observed co-failure never create an edge.

local_benign_update.definition: One content-addressed, reversible agent-side procedural rule generated from the target failure slice and target ConstraintSpec only. The updater may not see non-target outcomes or topology labels. Benign means target-scoped intent/content, not that future effects are assumed safe or beneficial.
scope_controls: exact bytes reused inside same-update pairs

constructs.update_target: The unique preregistered target ConstraintSpec c_i supplied to the updater. A scientific unit is eligible only under preregistered pre-update criteria; no post-update result can change target identity.

metrics.target_repair_gain: TRG_i = phi_i(update replay) - phi_i(no-update counterfactual replay), aggregated only under the preregistered estimator.
metrics.spontaneous_regression_control: CRR0_i uses an otherwise identical no-update reset/replay; update-attributable externality is CRR_i - CRR0_i.
metrics.update_externality: UE_i = CRR_update_i - CRR_no_update_i. Negative values are retained rather than clipped.
metrics.propagation_profile: P(d) = Pr(non-target regression | shortest-path distance(target,j)=d, baseline satisfied), with shared-resource exposure reported alongside distance.

topology_contract.independent: Same constraint count; target and non-target obligations use disjoint mutable resources and no prerequisite path.
topology_contract.chain: Directed prerequisite/read-after-write sequence c1 -> c2 -> ... using benchmark-semantic dependencies.
topology_contract.hub: Target or a fixed central obligation shares a real state/API dependency with multiple non-target obligations.
topology_contract.cycle: NOT_PRIMARY; allowed only if an actual benchmark workflow has a semantically valid directed cycle before outcomes.

competing_hypotheses.name: UPDATE_MAGNITUDE
competing_hypotheses.prediction: Larger update artifacts explain collateral regression; with exact same-update pairing or magnitude matching, topology effect should vanish.

competing_hypotheses.name: CONSTRAINT_COUNT
competing_hypotheses.prediction: Number of obligations, not their interaction structure, explains regression; at fixed count topology contributes no residual effect.

competing_hypotheses.name: TASK_DIFFICULTY
competing_hypotheses.prediction: Harder tasks both trigger repair and regress more; after preregistered baseline-difficulty matching topology effect vanishes.

competing_hypotheses.name: UPDATE_SURFACE
competing_hypotheses.prediction: A particular update surface may be intrinsically risky. The primary experiment cannot test this by switching surfaces; the surface is frozen and this remains a later generalization hypothesis.

competing_hypotheses.name: CONSTRAINT_COUPLING_EXTERNALITY
competing_hypotheses.prediction: After fixing count, update bytes/magnitude, pre-update difficulty, backbone, harness, and update surface, graph coupling to the target still predicts newly violated non-target constraints; regression risk should decline with target-graph distance or increase with shared-resource exposure.

competing_hypotheses.name: CAPABILITY_MASKING
competing_hypotheses.prediction: A stronger executor may suppress observed regressions through compensation, while a weak executor may create floor effects; capability must be prequalified on a disjoint calibration split and cannot be changed after decisive outcomes.

decisive_experiment.name: MATCHED_LOCAL_REPAIR_EXTERNALITY
decisive_experiment.substrate: AppWorld-Externality (benchmark-derived controlled train/dev task family; not official leaderboard)
decisive_experiment.unit: A repair family r contains one frozen source failure, one frozen candidate update u_r, and matched composite probe worlds whose target obligation is held fixed while non-target coupling is assigned outcome-blind.
same_update_design: Use a target-only or target-isolated repair-source episode to create exactly one failure slice and candidate u_r before any post-update probe outcomes are opened.
Freeze u_r by SHA-256; identical bytes, injection position, retrieval/exposure rule, backbone, and harness are reused in every topology arm for that repair family.

Generate independent/chain/hub composite probes from task-generator metadata before model outcomes, matching constraint count, instruction-template budget, difficulty stratum, app/tool budget, and target obligation.
Run frozen pre-update probes from checkpointed initial state to establish target/non-target baseline constraint vector under preregistered eligibility rules.
For each eligible probe, reset to the exact initial state and run a no-update counterfactual replay; separately reset and run the update replay.

Measure target gain, per-constraint new violations, update-attributable externality, and graph-distance/shared-resource propagation. Keep all zero/negative target gains; do not select updates by post-update success.
decisive_experiment.primary_estimand: Within-repair-family difference in update-attributable non-target regression between coupled and independent topology arms, with the exact same u_r. A hierarchical constraint-level model may estimate beta_coupling while repair-family effects absorb update-specific variance.
required_controls: same candidate update within paired family
matched pre-update difficulty under disjoint calibration rules
same reset snapshot within a probe
not_allowed: choose u_r after seeing collateral outcomes
drop zero-gain or harmful updates after post-update observation
change update surface across primary arms
change model because an effect is weak
use terminal success as the only endpoint

causal_language_rule: Correlation of observed graph statistics with regression is diagnostic. Causal propagation language is allowed only for the preregistered topology manipulation/randomized-isomorphic matched construction; where regression occurs is not by itself why regression occurs.

H5_clear_falsifiers: In same-update matched pairs, coupled and independent arms have no practically meaningful difference under the preregistered equivalence/non-inferiority region, and graph distance has no ordered relationship with regression.
Any apparent topology effect disappears when exact shared mutable-resource exposure is held fixed, showing that the chosen graph label adds no mechanism beyond a simpler exposure count.
Update magnitude, constraint count, or pre-update difficulty explains the effect while beta_coupling is null under preregistered controls.
Graph-disconnected constraints regress at the same update-attributable rate as graph-near constraints across repair families.
falsification.if_H5_fails: Do not create Coupling-Aware Update Scoping as a contribution. Adjudicate mechanism failure and either reformulate around the surviving competing explanation or stop.

capability_masking.rule: Backbone choice occurs only after substrate qualification and from a disjoint capability-calibration protocol. The decisive causal contrast stays within one fixed backbone.
capability_masking.floor_rule: If the chosen model cannot satisfy enough non-target baseline constraints or cannot execute core AppWorld tasks on the disjoint qualification split, declare capability floor and do not infer absence or presence of coupling.
capability_masking.ceiling_rule: If the chosen model almost never produces target failures or compensates all perturbations on the disjoint qualification split, move to a preregistered harder stratum or alternate predeclared backbone before opening decisive outcomes; never switch after seeing the topology estimate.
capability_masking.validation_model: A second capability level is external-validity validation only after the primary mechanism decision.

mechanism_derived_method_hypothesis.name: COUPLING_AWARE_UPDATE_SCOPING
mechanism_derived_method_hypothesis.pipeline: Failure -> Candidate Update -> Constraint Dependency Graph -> Affected Closure -> Scoped Update -> Counterfactual Regression Check -> Commit/Reject
mechanism_derived_method_hypothesis.activation_condition: Only after qualified evidence supports H5.

pre_f0_questions.1_best_substrate: AppWorld-Externality, a controlled extension of AppWorld train/dev with AppWorld-UL semantics as reference.
pre_f0_questions.2_why_better: It uniquely combines realistic multi-app state, controllable local databases, checkpoints, task generators, collateral-damage unit tests, and strong audience relevance.
pre_f0_questions.3_longitudinal_persistent_update: Not native; identifiable by an explicit agent-side procedural artifact that persists while each world replay is reset. This extension is part of the scientific contract.
pre_f0_questions.4_true_constraint: A semantic obligation/invariant compiled to a programmatic predicate, not an arbitrary raw assertion count.
pre_f0_questions.5_edge_definition: Static shared mutable resource, shared state-changing API resource, or prerequisite dependency only; never outcome-derived.
pre_f0_questions.6_outcome_blind_topology: Yes, via task-generator/evaluator metadata and pre-generated matched task families before model execution.
pre_f0_questions.7_local_benign_update: One target-only, content-addressed, reversible procedural repair note with no non-target outcome or topology access.
pre_f0_questions.8_update_target: One preregistered target ConstraintSpec c_i that defines updater input and target gain.
pre_f0_questions.9_programmatic_collateral: Baseline-satisfied non-target predicates that newly fail on update replay, differenced against a no-update reset replay.
pre_f0_questions.10_same_update_possible: Yes, by generating u_r once per repair-source episode and reusing exact bytes across matched topology probes.
pre_f0_questions.11_vs_magnitude: Exact same-update pairs make update byte/token/clause magnitude identical; remaining across-family magnitude is a covariate or stratum, not the topology intervention.
pre_f0_questions.12_vs_forgetting: The prediction is target-centered and graph-structured: regression risk varies with predeclared coupling/distance from a targeted local update. Generic old-task decline without this structure does not support H5.
pre_f0_questions.13_model_strength: Use disjoint capability calibration, predeclared floor/ceiling rules, one primary backbone for identification, and one later validation backbone.
pre_f0_questions.14_external_collision: Broad misevolution, forgetting, continual-skill, and skill-harm collisions exist; no direct same-update constraint-topology test was located in the bounded audit. Claim must remain narrow.
pre_f0_questions.15_internal_collision: Surface routing, admission, lifecycle uptake, memory interaction, temporal safety, and proxy-reward objects are explicitly excluded from the principal claim.
pre_f0_questions.16_falsifier: No topology/distance residual in same-update matched arms after controls, or collapse to a simpler shared-resource exposure/count explanation, falsifies H5.

A_INTERNAL_NOVELTY_RESIDUAL.note: Passes only with fixed update surface and post-validity/uptake starting boundary.

B_EXTERNAL_NOVELTY_RESIDUAL.note: No direct collision located in bounded audit; broad side-effect/forgetting/skill-harm claims are forbidden.

C_QUALIFIED_AGENT_SUBSTRATE.note: AppWorld engine/evaluator qualifies; persistent-update experiment requires explicitly labeled benchmark-derived controlled extension.

D_PERSISTENT_UPDATE_IDENTIFIABLE.note: One agent-side procedural artifact persists; environment state is reset.

E_CONSTRAINT_GRAPH_IDENTIFIABLE.note: ConstraintSpec compiler plus static resource/prerequisite edges.

F_COLLATERAL_OUTCOME_PROGRAMMATIC.note: Per-constraint evaluator predicates plus no-update replay.

G_UPDATE_TARGET_IDENTIFIABLE.note: Unique target ConstraintSpec before post-update outcomes.

H_UPDATE_MAGNITUDE_CONTROL_IDENTIFIABLE.note: Exact same artifact bytes within decisive pair; token/byte/clause fields across families.

I_GENERIC_FORGETTING_DISTINGUISHABLE.note: Requires target-centered graph-distance/coupling prediction, not aggregate old-task decline.

J_CAPABILITY_MASKING_RULES_DEFINED.note: Disjoint calibration and frozen model after outcome opening.

K_DECISIVE_EXPERIMENT_IDENTIFIABLE.note: Same-update matched topology plus no-update counterfactual reset/replay.

L_3D_PAPER_BOUNDARY_PASS.note: Independent dataset, model, metric, intervention, evidence, and principal claim contract.

M_AUTHORITY_ZERO.note: No provider, GPU, P0/P1, method, or scientific execution authority granted.

N_NO_SCIENTIFIC_OUTCOME_USED.note: Only literature facts and static source/schema inspection were used.

paper_story_hypothesis_level: Self-evolving agents increasingly retain and reuse experience.
Existing evaluation often emphasizes whether adaptation improves later performance.
A target-local repair may also alter behavior beyond its intended target.
Raw update size or constraint count need not identify this interference.
We test whether structural coupling among constraints predicts update externality.
A controlled realistic substrate separates target gain from collateral regression.
The decisive design reuses the same candidate update across matched interaction contexts.
Propagation is decomposed by graph distance and shared-resource exposure.
A coupling-aware scoping method is considered only if the mechanism survives.
If unsupported, the mechanism is falsified or reformulated rather than forced into a method claim.

stop_or_reformulate_if: Direct prior work is found that already identifies the same same-update topology mechanism.
Constraint edges cannot be defined without outcomes.
Same-update topology manipulation cannot be made without changing target repair semantics.
Per-constraint evaluator cannot separate new non-target violations from terminal failure.
Apparent topology reduces completely to count, magnitude, difficulty, or a simpler shared-resource exposure explanation under preregistered controls.
reopen_execution_discussion_only_after: Pre-F0 artifact/test integrity holds on the live canonical.
AppWorld exact data/bundle license and revision are verified.
Constraint compiler produces outcome-blind matched families in static/non-scientific preflight.
Backbone capability qualification protocol is frozen.
Explicit separate provider/GPU/scientific execution authority is granted.
